- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after bullish sentiment events or high supply net events; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such contexts.
- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of upward momentum to forecast.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model overcorrects and underestimates subsequent peaks; apply a 1–2 day “overshoot buffer” to avoid premature decline.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model exhibits mean reversion bias; shift forecast 1–2% higher to account for persistent bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% to reflect market resilience.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment if recent sentiment or event context shows strong bullish momentum.
